thread.title: Apple's stock goes ex-dividend, slips toward 1st loss in 10 days

author: morningstar.com
title: Apple's stock goes ex-dividend, slips toward 1st loss in 10 days
text:
Apple Inc.'s stock (AAPL) slipped 0.4% in morning trade Friday, putting it in danger of suffering its first loss in 10 sessions. The nine-session win streak through Thursday, which was the longest such streak since the nine-day stretch ending July 19, 2017 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-stock-surges-toward-biggest-6-day-rally-in-9-years-2018-05-07), and Thursday's fifth-straight record close, were fueled by better-than-expected earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-surprise-in-apple-earnings-big-growth-in-china-2018-05-01) and an endorsement from famed billionaire value investor Warren Buffett (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/warren-buffetts-berkshire-hathaway-bought-75-million-apple-shares-in-first-quarter-2018-05-03). The stock closed at a record $190.04 on Thursday. For those wondering why, with the stock trading at $188.74, some quoting services say its trading down just 57 cents from $189.31, it's because the stock went ex-dividend. That means the quoting services adjusted the close to reflect the payout of a 73-cent quarterly dividend. The stock has rallied 11.6% year to date, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has gained 0.4%.
-Tomi Kilgore; 1139ET
